Root: P(churn)=sigmoid(-2.449 + sum of the six children's readouts). Purely additive in the logit: linear backbone + CSC threshold + day/eve usage hinge + day-charge hinges + low-day x low-intl interaction + affine offsets. 31 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries.

No child gates another; 31 unconnected inputs (26 states, area codes 408 and 415, day/eve/night call counts) have zero effect. Train AUC 0.9113 vs refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433 and the all-children-linearised network 0.8327. Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto the all-linear model: linear_backbone +0.0, csc_threshold +0.0393, day_eve_hinge +0.0604, day_charge_cluster +0.0069, intl_lowday_interaction +0.0169, affine_offsets +0.0. The model treats a higher total daytime minutes as clearly raising the predicted chance that a customer leaves in an uneven way: for a typical customer, it goes from about 1% at 112 minutes to about 15% at 249 minutes, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower.

The model treats a higher voice-mail messages as raising the predicted chance that a customer leaves steadily: for a typical customer, it goes from about 2% at 0 messages to about 10% at 32 messages, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower (on the training data only).

A higher total daytime minutes clearly raises the predicted chance that a customer leaves, and even more so if total evening minutes is above 201 minutes (in an uneven way for patients with total evening minutes above 201 minutes): for a typical customer, total daytime minutes going from 112 minutes to 249 minutes moves the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 1% to about 40% if total evening minutes is above 201 minutes, and from about 1% to about 4% if total evening minutes is at or below 201 minutes.

Through one part of the model, total daytime charge only clearly lowers the predicted chance that a customer leaves while it stays below about 35.84 US dollars (between 35.84 and 40.40 US dollars for different customers): for a typical such customer, going from 15.49 US dollars to 59.76 US dollars moves it from about 6% to about 1%.
The model ignores total daytime calls, total evening calls and total night-time calls.
